summary: PASS. Both items carried forward from round 2 are fixed and I re-verified every rule from scratch rather than trusting prior rounds. (1) The R39/PF7 P1 is fixed: conandata.yml at HEAD and in the working tree name only the official upstream URL https://github.com/M4444/TMatrix/archive/refs/tags/v1.4.tar.gz; the shipped tarball /root/tm-src/gh.tar.gz hashes to exactly the declared 99591915fa83ceb98c31a97b5686a2df0d667c5d62f3e82837f76e5f9243710e; no conandata.yml.orig/.bak/.rej exists in the package dir or in git; and git grep for mirror/gh-proxy/netdisk over the tracked package returns nothing. I confirmed the root cause is ci/conan/build_and_test.sh:1019-1054 (the 'Mirror fallback' step injects gh-proxy.com and leaves a .orig with no restore anywhere) and filed that as P2, framework-scoped and forbidden to a collaborator PR by review-memory rule 21, with the caveat that it will recur. (2) The stale docstring is fixed: conanfile.py now describes the two genuine FindCurses failure modes (hard failure with 'Could NOT find Curses (missing: CURSES_LIBRARY)', or success contributing the archive with no include dir so #include <ncurses.h> fails), and the recipe sets zero CURSES_* variables. notes.md:71 and manifest.yaml:72 still mention CURSES_LIBRARY but both are conditional framings of FindCurses behaviour ('can only find the archive IF the recipe seeds...', 'it locates A seeded CURSES_LIBRARY but...'), not assertions that the shipped recipe seeds it, so I did not raise them. Re-verified independently: R32 (settings.os in Linux/OHOS), R33 (no bare CC/CFLAGS/CXX/LDFLAGS anywhere), R34 (test_package genuinely executes the packaged OHOS ELF through qemu-aarch64), R38 (software-level commands.json, type=tool, ref tmatrix/1.4), R8 (no __OHOS__ or platform conditional in the patch), L0a-L0e (conanfile.py + real test source + MANIFEST.yml all present), L0g (name/version/4 settings/license/description, version '1.4' matches the directory, conandata carries a sha256), R19 (9 tracked files, all text, 897 insertions, no binaries), R37, R26 (binary NEEDs only libc.so, ncurses statically linked). The patch applies cleanly (patch -p1 --dry-run rc=0, real apply rc=0, no rejects) to a byte-identical pristine upstream tree and the result is byte-identical to the manifest's declared work dir; manifest's source_orig_hash/source_work_hash reproduce exactly using the repo's own _compute_hash, so the earlier apparent mismatch was mine (I had compared single-file hashes) and is not a defect. Mutation testing proves all 8 unconditional assertions can fail: a silent stub fails all 9, a stub printing the rejection diagnostics passes only T3/T4/T6c, a stub printing a version string plus an ESC passes only T1/T6, and an x86-64 ELF or a zero-byte file fails T7, whose ELF-header byte offsets I checked by hand. The destructive negatives also hold at the Conan level: hiding bin/tmatrix exits 6, corrupting e_machine exits 1 with 8 assertions / 1 failure, so notes.md:230's L1e claim is true and the gate cannot be gamed. Measured counts are 8 assertions / 0 failures / T6b SKIP as root (both via the requested direct invocation and via a real 'conan test test_package tmatrix/1.4'), and 9 assertions / 0 failures / T6b PASS as an unprivileged uid with a reachable terminfo database; the suite also runs clean under dash. These match MANIFEST.yml (test_package_test_count 9, assertion_count 8) and notes.md (8 as root, 9 unprivileged) exactly, so the documentation does not overstate. I additionally re-verified the accepted TERMINFO deviation behaviourally (a tmatrix-only consumer exports only PATH and no TERMINFO; adding ncurses/6.6 yields TERMINFO=/root/.conan2/p/ncurs780a5e6acf3cf/p/share/terminfo, which really contains x/xterm), that manifest status 'built' is honest, and that the notes.md CI-gate table's only checkable number is accurate (G0 = 541 .kv entries under knowledge/graph excluding _template/principles, exactly 541). Both conanfile.py files compile, all four YAML/JSON files parse, no CRLF, every file ends in a newline, no TODO/FIXME/XXX/请填写 placeholders, no committed .orig/.bak/.pyc/__pycache__ (the two local __pycache__ dirs are gitignored by .gitignore:204), and the test script contains no bashisms (no [[ ]], arrays, $'...', <<<, local or function; parses and passes under dash). Remaining items are 2 P2 (the live CI mirror mutation, and the absent software-level manifest.yaml which the user pre-classified) and 5 P3 nits (one unused import, one backwards-reading install-prefix comment whose behaviour I confirmed is nonetheless correct, one imprecise 'always executed' wording, one misclassified error type that still fails the gate, and the mirror form surviving in an unsquashed intermediate commit). None are blocking; no P0 and no P1 remain.

findings.description: The 'Mirror fallback' step (lines 1019-1054) rewrites conandata.yml in place, turning the official github.com url into a list whose first entry is 'https://gh-proxy.com/'+url, and writes a '${CONANDATA}.orig' backup. Grepping every reference to CONANDATA in the script shows NO restore of the mutated file anywhere afterwards (the only cp-back, at line 1183, restores an unrelated predownload mutation). This is the exact mechanism that produced the round-2 P1 and it is still live: the next local gate run on any GitHub-sourced package will silently re-dirty the working tree, and a subsequent 'git add -A' would re-commit the mirror. HEAD is clean, so nothing is currently shipped, and review-memory rule 21 forbids a collaborator PR from editing ci/, so this is correctly out of scope for this recipe PR and must be filed as a separate framework PR. Raised P2, not P1, because the delivered package at HEAD is correct.
findings.fix_suggestion: Separate framework PR: either make the mirror rewrite a non-destructive, ephemeral change (operate on a temp copy of conandata.yml, or restore it via a trap/cleanup on exit), or drop the gh-proxy.com entry from get_mirrors(). Also 'rm -f ${CONANDATA}.orig' in the same cleanup. Note *.orig is already in .gitignore (line 17), which is why only the mutated conandata.yml was ever committed.

findings.description: No software-level manifest.yaml exists at archives/t/tmatrix/manifest.yaml; only the per-version archives/t/tmatrix/1.4/manifest.yaml is present. review-memory rule 17 lists 'manifest.yaml / README.md' at the software level. The user pre-classified this as an accepted deviation (only ncurses and a handful of others have one) and directed it be rated P2 if raised at all. It is a genuine structural gap against the rule but carries no deception and no build impact.
findings.fix_suggestion: Either add a minimal software-level manifest.yaml, or record an explicit waiver in notes.md citing that the repo convention is to keep manifests at version level only. Non-blocking.

findings.description: 'import os' is never used: grep for 'os.' in conanfile.py returns 0 matches. The recipe uses no os module functionality (get() and the CMake helpers handle paths). Contrast test_package/conanfile.py, where os, platform and shutil are all genuinely used.

The comment reads 'Upstream defaults the install prefix to /usr; keep the package self-contained instead (R49 spirit: no writes to a shared prefix)' immediately above 'CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX = "/"'. On its face '/' is the least self-contained value, so the comment reads backwards. The behaviour is in fact correct and I verified it: Conan 2.29's CMake.install() runs 'cmake --install <build> --prefix <package_folder>', and the command-line --prefix overrides the cache variable, so the delivered tree is bin/tmatrix + share/... inside the package folder (confirmed against /root/.conan2/p/b/tmatr38f3a9677f48a/p, whose CMakeCache.txt does hold CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX:PATH=/ yet whose install landed in the package folder). The comment simply omits the reason, and it also fails to mention the second real effect: setting the cache var makes CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX_INITIALIZED_TO_DEFAULT false, which suppresses the upstream/patched 'set(CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX "/usr" CACHE PATH "..." FORCE)' block. No deception, but a reader cannot tell why the line is safe.
findings.fix_suggestion: Reword to name the mechanism, e.g.: 'Conan passes --prefix <package_folder> to cmake --install, so this cache value never lands on the real filesystem; setting it also stops the upstream CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX_INITIALIZED_TO_DEFAULT branch from force-setting /usr.' Consider also just deleting the line and relying on --prefix.

findings.description: The comment '8 always executed; T6b is conditional on a reachable terminfo database' is slightly overstated. In test_tmatrix.sh, T6, T6b and T6c are all nested inside 'if command -v script >/dev/null 2>&1' (line 156), so only T1-T5 and T7 (6 assertions) are unconditionally executed; T6 and T6c additionally require script(1), which does print a SKIP line at line 195. The documented numbers themselves are right: I measured 8 assertions / 0 failures / T6b SKIP as root and 9 assertions / 0 failures / T6b PASS as an unprivileged uid, matching assertion_count 8 and test_package_test_count 9 exactly. Only the word 'always' is imprecise.
findings.fix_suggestion: Reword to '6 unconditional; T6/T6c require script(1); T6b requires a reachable terminfo database. In the delivered CI image all 8 non-T6b assertions execute.'

findings.description: A missing packaged executable is an artifact/build failure, not a configuration problem, yet it raises ConanInvalidConfiguration. I checked whether this could mask the gate (it does not): with bin/tmatrix moved away, 'conan test test_package tmatrix/1.4' prints 'Invalid configuration: packaged tmatrix not found' and exits 6, and with a corrupted ELF the suite prints 8 assertions / 1 failure and exits 1. So notes.md:230's L1e claim ('moving bin/ away makes the test fail, proving it really depends on the package') is TRUE and the gate genuinely fails. The nit is purely that the message is classified 'Invalid configuration' rather than 'Error in test()', which a CI wrapper that treats those two categories differently could mishandle.
findings.fix_suggestion: Raise ConanException (or a plain RuntimeError) instead of ConanInvalidConfiguration so a missing artifact reports as a test error rather than an invalid configuration.

findings.description: HEAD (302baff5a0 'fix(tmatrix): restore official source URL...') is clean: 'git show HEAD:archives/t/tmatrix/1.4/conandata.yml' names only https://github.com/M4444/TMatrix/archive/refs/tags/v1.4.tar.gz, and the working tree matches HEAD byte-for-byte with no .orig/.bak/.rej anywhere. However the mirror form still exists in intermediate commit d4b143d2a3 on this local branch. Nothing is shipped (the branch is unmerged), but pushing the full branch history instead of squashing would leave a reachable commit containing 'https://gh-proxy.com/https://github.com/...'. This is informational only and does not affect the current state under review.
findings.fix_suggestion: Squash the four tmatrix commits into one before pushing, or push main + a single squashed commit, so no reachable history contains the mirror form.

previous_p1_status.original: R39/PF7: conandata.yml sources.url was a list whose first entry was the hand-added https://gh-proxy.com/ mirror injected by the ci/conan/build_and_test.sh 'Mirror fallback' step and accidentally committed.
previous_p1_status.evidence: git show HEAD:archives/t/tmatrix/1.4/conandata.yml (302baff5a0) yields exactly one url line: url: "https://github.com/M4444/TMatrix/archive/refs/tags/v1.4.tar.gz" - a plain scalar, not a list, with no mirror. The working tree is byte-identical to HEAD (git diff HEAD -- archives/t/tmatrix/ is empty), so nothing is dirty locally. git grep -niE 'gh-proxy|mirror|netdisk|pan\.|baidu|aliyun|nexus' over the tracked package returns no match. No conandata.yml.orig/.bak/.rej exists in archives/t/tmatrix/ (find returned empty) and none is tracked (git ls-files lists only the 9 intended text files). The source really is the official tarball: sha256sum /root/tm-src/gh.tar.gz = 99591915fa83ceb98c31a97b5686a2df0d667c5d62f3e82837f76e5f9243710e, matching conandata.yml and manifest.yaml exactly, at the 6324927 bytes conandata.yml's comment claims. The mirror form does survive in intermediate commit d4b143d2a3 on this unmerged local branch, which is why I logged a separate informational P3 recommending a squash before push; HEAD itself is clean.

previous_p1_status.original: Stale docstring: conanfile.py's module docstring asserted in the present tense that 'the recipe seeds CURSES_LIBRARY', which is untrue - the shipped recipe sets no CURSES_* variables.
previous_p1_status.evidence: conanfile.py lines 15-23 now read: 'The FindCurses module has no sysroot notion, so in this cross build it either fails outright ("Could NOT find Curses (missing: CURSES_LIBRARY)") or, once handed the archive, contributes that archive alone with no include path -- in which case `#include <ncurses.h>` fails to compile. Resolving the dependency through its CONFIG package carries both halves.' That is the two real failure modes. Cross-checked against the code: the only CURSES_* occurrences in conanfile.py are inside that docstring, and generate() sets just CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME, CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR and CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX - no CURSES_LIBRARY, CURSES_INCLUDE_DIR, CURSES_NEED_NCURSES or CURSES_LIBRARIES anywhere, confirmed by grep -rn 'CURSES' over the whole package. The recipe's own class is TmatrixConan (code-style rule 2 naming) and package_type is 'application' with bindirs set, as code-style rules 2 and 4 require.

patch was hand-written, not produced by refresh-patch --auto
